terminal_record.title: Trump Held an Iowa Veterans Fundraiser in January 2016 Instead of Attending a GOP Debate
terminal_record.description_short: Trump held a televised Iowa veterans fundraiser in January 2016 instead of attending a GOP debate; about $2.8 million went to the Trump Foundation.
terminal_record.description_medium: In January 2016, Trump held a televised Iowa fundraiser for veterans instead of attending a Republican debate. The event raised about $5.6 million, with roughly $2.8 million going to the Trump Foundation, according to contemporaneous reporting. The New York attorney general later said the Foundation had given Trump’s campaign control over those funds. In November 2019, a court separately ordered Trump to pay $2 million in damages.
terminal_record.description_long: In January 2016, Donald Trump held a televised Iowa fundraiser for veterans instead of attending a Republican debate. The event raised about $5.6 million. A contemporaneous account said about $2.8 million went to the Trump Foundation, while private donors gave the remainder directly to veterans’ charities. The New York attorney general later said Trump and the Foundation admitted that the event was a campaign event and that the Foundation gave the campaign control over the timing, amounts, and recipients of the $2.8 million raised through it. The attorney general’s case concerned the Foundation’s use of charitable assets for political purposes. In November 2019, a New York court ordered Trump to pay $2 million in damages. NPR reported that court documents said the Foundation’s $2.82 million from the fundraiser was used for Trump’s campaign and disbursed by campaign staff, rather than by the Foundation; it also reported that the money eventually reached charities supporting veterans. The 2019 damages order was the later resolution of the Foundation case, not an event that took place on the fundraiser date.
